articles.title: Samsung's Processing-in-Memory (PIM)
articles.summary: Samsung is implementing Processing-in-Memory (PIM) technology within their LPDDR5X chips, which can utilize the internal bandwidth of the memory chip to access data from multiple banks simultaneously, resulting in a significant increase in throughput. This allows for the use of standard LPDDR5X protocol while exposing compute capabilities that aren't part of the memory interface. The PIM blocks consist of a MAC tree with surrounding register files and control logic, and can sustain up to eight MAC operations per cycle. This technology has the potential to significantly increase aggregate compute throughput, but its implementation may be expensive due to the need for multiple chips.
